items.preg: When I am truly angry with someone, I feel tense but comfortable because I expressed exactly what I was thinking.
When I am truly angry with someone, I feel anxious and confused about what I should say.
When I am truly angry with someone, I feel hostile and want to confront them verbally.
When I am truly angry with someone, I think I should not express my anger directly.
When I am truly angry with someone, I think: "well, I am angry, but I should handle this constructively."
When I am truly angry with someone, I think I should confront them and forcefully show my anger.
When I am truly angry with someone, I express what bothered me and try to reach a constructive solution.
When I am truly angry with someone, I express my anger and get into an argument.
When I am truly angry with someone, I say nothing so as not to hurt their feelings.
When someone is truly angry with me, I feel tense and feel that I have the right to understand the reason for their anger, responding to them directly.
When someone is truly angry with me, I feel angry, hostile, and want to strike back.
When someone is truly angry with me, I feel confused, afraid, and want to withdraw.
When someone is truly angry with me, I think I probably did something wrong and that person does not like me.
When someone is truly angry with me, I think I have to respond even more forcefully so I do not end up defeated.
When someone is truly angry with me, I think I should understand the reason for their anger and respond to them directly to resolve the conflict.
When someone is truly angry with me, I behave by expressing my anger and intensifying the argument.
When someone is truly angry with me, I ask for an explanation of their anger and openly address our feelings.
When someone is truly angry with me, I behave by backing down, offering excuses, and not expressing what I really feel.
When I communicate with a person who has "authority," I feel I have to be on the defensive and try to find the right strategy to approach them.
When I communicate with a person who has "authority," I feel comfortable and approach them directly.
When I communicate with a person who has "authority," I feel nervous and unsure about how to approach them.
When I communicate with a person who has "authority," I think I really should not bother them or take up their time.
When I communicate with a person who has "authority," I think what I want or need is so important that I can impose my point of view.
When I communicate with a person who has "authority," I think my needs are legitimate and that it is right for me to express them frankly.
When I communicate with a person who has authority, I act awkwardly and make excuses.
When I communicate with a person who has authority, I behave in a comfortable and calm manner.
When I communicate with a person who has "authority," I behave defensively and even somewhat aggressively.
When someone asks me for something important, I feel nervous and anxious not to give the impression that I want to refuse.
When someone asks me for something important, I feel comfortable saying "yes" or "no."
When someone asks me for something important, I feel annoyed that they expect me to agree.
When someone asks me for something important, I think I have the right to say "yes" or "no" and I feel comfortable with either option.
When someone asks me for something important, I think I do not want anything imposed on me and so I refuse, even if that is not how I really feel.
When someone asks me for something important, I say "yes" even though I should say "no."
When someone asks me for something important, I behave defensively and refuse, or make it clear that I disliked their request and then comply reluctantly.
When someone asks me for something important, I behave according to my true feelings and frankly tell them "yes" or "no."
When someone asks me for something important, I react by agreeing to what they ask even though I do not want to.
When I ask someone for something important, I feel anxious or reluctant to approach them.
When I ask someone for something important, I am more inclined to do what suits me than to respect the other person's feelings.
When I ask someone for something important, I feel confident and comfortable asserting my right to make the request.
When I ask someone for something important, I think what I need or want is important, so the person should respond immediately.
When I ask someone for something important, I think I really should not be bothering them with my request.
When I ask someone for something important, I think I have the right to do so, but that I will respect how the person decides to respond.
When I ask someone for something important, I do it in an exaggerated and insistent way.
When I ask someone for something important, I behave calmly and make my request openly.
When I ask someone for something important, I behave hesitantly and awkwardly when making my request.
When I am in a new group of people and need to start communicating, I feel anxious and confused about how to do it.
When I am in a new group of people and need to start communicating, I feel comfortable.
When I am in a new group of people and need to start communicating, I feel uncomfortable and pressured, but I initiate the communication anyway.
When I am in a new group of people and need to start communicating, I think it will be interesting to get to know each other better.
When I am in a new group of people and need to start communicating, I think I should do it whether or not the group is ready.
When I am in a new group of people and need to start communicating, I think they are more relaxed than I am and that, anyway, I do not have much to say to them.
When I am in a new group of people and need to start communicating, I behave cautiously and wait until someone speaks to me.
When I am in a new group of people and need to start communicating, I tend to talk a lot and even tend to come across as annoying.
When I am in a new group of people and need to start communicating, I behave calmly, introduce myself to someone who seems interesting, or simply mingle.
I am a cheerful person.
I solve my problems easily.
I am satisfied with the way I relate to others.
My voice is clear and others hear it.
My relationships with other people are easy and comfortable.
I am a person who cares about others, and it seems they sense that about me.
My everyday life is full of things that keep me interested.
I find it difficult to talk with people who have authority.
I feel I can make up my mind very easily.
I feel that I am an important person.
I feel that my feelings are not easily hurt.
I am trustworthy and I can really depend on myself.
It seems I do not care what might happen to me.
I am confident in my ability to communicate easily and effectively with other people.
I know when I should speak and when I should listen.
I can understand and be patient with a person who is going through an emotional crisis.
I can ask my friends to help me, even if I cannot return the favor.
I feel that it is very difficult to speak in front of a group of people.
I face and solve problems as they arise, instead of avoiding them and putting them off.
I am a self-confident person.
I enjoy creating new interpersonal relationships, and I can describe myself as someone who cares about others.
People easily get me to change my mind, even after I have already made a decision.
I get impatient with others easily.
My nonverbal communication (eyes, facial expression, movements) facilitates my communication with others.
I am an affectionate and open person, so people feel comfortable telling me their concerns and personal feelings.
I am the kind of person people can really tell their personal problems to.
If given the opportunity, I could be an effective leader.
I like myself and feel satisfied with the kind of person I am.
I am afraid of being myself.
I enjoy social gatherings just for the sake of being with people.
Because I am shy, I find it difficult to stand up for my rights.
I am excited about myself and about the potential I can develop as a person.
I believe I should say what I feel when dealing with other people.
I know how to ask for a favor without imposing myself.
My friends tell me I am an understanding person.
I feel others' emotions the way they do.
For me, everything is possible if I believe in myself.
I trust my ability to evaluate a situation that arises.
I can describe myself as a creative person.
I can handle the ups and downs of work.
I feel comfortable showing my weaknesses to my friends.
I am free to be myself and can handle the consequences.
My handshake is confident and firm, and conveys a strong personality to others.
I know how close I can get to another person without making them feel uncomfortable.
I have the ability to listen and truly understand other people's feelings.
Others consider me good at listening to them.
Living for the future gives my life its main meaning.
For me, work and fun are equally important in my life.
I am assertive in my relationships with other people.
I feel I have control over my life.
I have the ability to change or grow in the way I consider appropriate for myself.
I can accept my mistakes instead of worrying about them.
I can decide how friendly to be with a stranger.
I can decide whether I should introduce myself to others or wait for someone else to introduce me.
I can understand how a person feels when they are talking with me.
When a person is telling me something important, I really focus on listening to them.
The future seems hopeful to me.
I am able to accept others as they are.
I regret many things I have done in the past.
In my daily routine I experience changes and new things.
I am able to discuss points of view that are contrary to my own.
I am able to praise those I admire.
I have the ability to feel comfortable with all kinds of people.
I know when it is appropriate to give another person a pat on the shoulder.
It seems I am able to sense precisely how another person feels.
When someone tells me how they feel, I can listen to them and understand their point of view.
I am an open, honest, and spontaneous person.
I am regarded by others as a leader.
I am able to create new friendships or relationships.
I set clear goals related to my career or my life.
When I carry out a task, I frequently evaluate my progress and get concrete feedback from the person in charge.
I am more likely to make a decision and act than to keep worrying about which alternative to take and get tense.
I have the ability to organize myself, following an efficient personal schedule.
I can get a group to agree with me when it is something that matters a great deal to me.
I intentionally work on building the future I want for myself.
When I get involved in a task, I sometimes think about how I would feel if I fail.
When I am part of a work team, I like to ensure that plans are carried out efficiently.
I make my decisions independently, and I rarely ask bosses, teachers, friends, or family for help.
I am able to set goals for myself and achieve them within a specific period of time.
I have the ability to make a strong, positive impact on most of the people I meet.
I try to incorporate challenges into my life.
I prefer challenging activities—that is, those that involve risk or the possibility of failure.
I devote most of my time and energy to important projects.
I have established a process that guides me in making important decisions.
I have the ability to plan and finish my work on schedule.
I am able to be persuasive (to convince) without taking advantage of others.
I take risks that get me out of monotony.
I am willing to take on projects that involve some risk of failing.
I know how to set my own goals.
If I am involved in a group project, I can suggest solutions that the other members accept.
If I were evaluated in terms of effectiveness at work, I would receive a high score for how I manage my time.
I feel comfortable approaching another person with the idea of selling them something.
I seek out new activities, even if they do not make me feel comfortable or secure.
I think more about success than about failure when I start a new task.
I think that despite the uncertainty of the future, it is worthwhile to make plans.
Changes in my life cause me conflict.
I waste little time.
If the team I belong to needs someone to speak for everyone, they tend to choose me.
Learning or doing new things fills me with enthusiasm.
When I am immersed in a difficult task, I think about all the resources I have available to complete it successfully.
I feel that my current work is satisfying.
When I face a difficult situation, I am able to see several alternatives and make a good decision.
I know exactly how much time I need to finish tasks and projects.
I can take charge of a situation when necessary.
I enjoy the emotions that changes bring out in me.
When I am working on a difficult task, I try to correct those personal weaknesses that might interfere with its successful completion.
I prefer projects that require intense effort or a long-term commitment.
Future trends are a matter of indifference to me.
I am an efficient and well-organized person.
Because I am a convincing and credible person, my friends tend to ask me to "talk" with someone instead of doing it themselves.
I dare to make mistakes.
I think that planning future activities does not take away from what makes life interesting.
I can concentrate on a task for a long period of time.
My decisions tend to be accepted as "good" by the people involved.
I am able to manage my time in the present so I do not feel pressured by the things I left undone.
My friends involve me in solving their problems.
I innovate.
My tendency is not to give in easily when I face a difficult problem.
On projects I am assigned, I prefer to work with a "subject-matter expert" rather than with a friend or acquaintance.
My friends tend to ask me for help when making important decisions.
I am among the first to arrive at meetings or events.
I am a good salesperson (promoter of my ideas).
If I fail, I try again.
I have the ability to stay with a job even when I no longer feel like it.
I finish what I start.
I am able to decide when a tense or difficult situation requires immediate action.
I arrive on time for my commitments.
I tend to talk with people who have differences so they can resolve their problems.
I am open to new ideas.
I am able to set priorities and reach the proposed objectives efficiently.
I have enough energy throughout the day to do what I have to do.
I am sure of the decisions I make.
I am able to work on several projects at the same time, with good results.
It seems I am able to "sell my image" to people with authority, by being just as I am.
I get excited about setting personal goals that are difficult to reach.
I achieve what I set out to do.
I intensely desire to succeed in what I set out to do.
I make decisions easily and with good results.
I have the ability to control my responsibilities instead of being controlled by them.
I am unable to calm others in tense situations.
I can change the course of my life easily if I consider it necessary.
When I start a difficult task, I am more motivated by thinking about success than about failure.
I am considered a reliable and responsible person.
I believe that, even though I have worked hard, I have not gotten as far as I can or want to because my education or my work has not given me the opportunity.
I believe that I have not been able to find the time to truly enjoy life the way I would like.
I am worried about some physical symptoms I have, such as headaches, insomnia, an ulcer, or high blood pressure.
When something needs to be done, people look for me.
I get impatient watching someone trying to do something that I can do much faster.
I am a tense person.
I feel physically healthy and full of energy.
I have worked hard to finish projects by the set deadline, the agreed date, or one I imposed on myself.
I find it difficult to unwind and have fun.
I am not able to comfortably express strong emotions, such as fear, anger, or sadness.
I sleep poorly.
I have a strong sense of what is good or bad for me, and I behave accordingly.
If I really calmed down and enjoyed life the way I would like, I would feel uncomfortable with myself.
Even when I am on vacation or simply resting and having fun, I put pressure on myself trying to meet goals.
I do things that are harmful to my health.
I am confident in my ability to create a good life for myself.
I want people to talk faster, and I find myself wanting to hurry them along.
I can relax at the end of a long day and then fall asleep easily.
I have healthy and nutritious eating habits.
When I decide to do something, I carry it out.
I perceive that I do not have control over what I think, feel, or do.
I am not able to relax naturally, so I tend to depend on other things to do so.
I do not get tired easily, because I have enough physical vigor.
I live my life according to my own personal values.
I feel tense and pressured by the way I have to live.
My coworkers and friends advise me to rest and relax.
I exercise regularly to stay in good physical condition.
In almost every kind of activity I carry out, I am able to perform well.
I get impatient with myself and with others, and I tend to push to speed things up.
I am under such tension that I can feel it in my body.
I am a healthy person and I take care of myself physically and emotionally.
I am a good worker, even when I am not supervised.
My friends tend to tell me that I look worried, tense, or nervous.
I handle tension well, and I have learned several healthy ways to relax.
I picture myself living a long and healthy life.
People admire my ability to achieve what I set out to do.
In my work I have a lot of tension.
I have been unable to break my negative habits that are a problem for me.
Many of my behaviors tend to be harmful to my health.
I fulfill my tasks and obligations, even when I encounter difficulties.
When I truly rest and do absolutely nothing for several days, I tend to feel guilty for having wasted so much time.
I get extremely nervous and tense, and doctors have recommended that I slow down and calm myself.
I wake up fresh and rested in the mornings.
I tend not to fail at things that seem important to me.
It seems I am continually striving to achieve results, but I do not take the time to honestly ask myself what I really want in life.
I apply procedures that allow me to manage my tensions effectively, such as rest techniques, exercise, or meditation.
I perceive that, compared with other people my age, I am sickly.
